subject: Requesting resilience rider & order form alignment for HeliosDX
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Susan Brooks <susan.brooks@heliosdx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Resilience rider & order form alignment for HeliosDX

Hi Susan —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, Helios is looking for a short resilience rider (SLA addendum) paired with a small set of order-form edits so the uptime/latency commitments and credits are visible to procurement and our legal team.

To make progress quickly, I’ve attached: 1) our first-pass redlines to the MSA, 2) a draft resilience rider that proposes the availability tiers and credit schedule, and 3) an order-form JSON that maps the products to the uptime bands.

Two asks to prioritize:
- Confirm Helios’ target availability band (you mentioned 99.95% across US regions) and whether cross-region failover is required for the order form.
- If procurement wants a fast review, can they share a preferred DocuSign route? We can produce a clean rider for signature once terms are agreed.

I’ve looped in Marissa to capture any technical acceptance criteria (telemetry/runbook evidence) that Procurement might require. Kimberly, can you flag any commercial items that we shouldn’t accept wholesale in the rider?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that moves things faster.

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[sent from mobile]

[Attachments: Helios_MSA_redlines_v1.pdf (pdf), Resilience_Rider_Draft.docx (docx), Orderform_HeliosDX_v0.9.json (json)]

From: Susan Brooks <susan.brooks@heliosdx.com>

Cc: Helios Diagnostics Procurement <procurement@heliosdx.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Resilience rider & order form alignment for HeliosDX

Sergio —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. Procurement confirms they’re aiming for 99.95% monthly availability, with regional failover preferred but not mandatory for the pilot. Two items from our side:

1) Latency objective: we need P50 < 120ms and P95 < 350ms for inference calls in our primary region during normal load windows.
2) Evidence: procurement will require a telemetry extract for the pilot month and a one-time runbook that shows our failover test plan.

Procurement copied on this thread (procurement@heliosdx.com) — can you prepare a clean resilience rider + order form with those numbers and indicate what evidence we can provide? Prefer DocuSign; procurement will send a routing once we have the final doc.

Best,
Susan Brooks
VP, Cloud Operations | Helios Diagnostics

Thanks for the loop, Sergio. Quick technical notes to include in the rider/order form:

- The latency objectives Susan listed are achievable for the sample workloads Helios described, but P95 at 350ms will depend on sequence lengths and whether they use streaming. We should limit the quoted SLA to inference calls with input tokens <= 512 and response length <= 256 tokens, or call out an exception.
- For cross-region failover: we can offer an optional regional-fallback configuration in the order form that adds a 10% uplift to the monthly commitment or a dedicated failover pool as a paid add-on.
- Evidence we can provide: aggregated telemetry exports (token-level latency histograms), daily availability reports for the pilot months, and a signed runbook template that Helios can use during their on-call exercises.

I’ll annotate the draft rider with the sequence-length caveat and the telemetry artifact list.

—Marissa
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

[Attachment reference: proposed telemetry schema sample (CSV) — will attach separately if legal okays]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Resilience rider & order form alignment for HeliosDX

Team —

I reviewed the attached redlines. High-level legal points:

- We should avoid hard availability guarantees tied to specific latency percentiles across all payloads; instead, define availability for successful request completion and a separate performance objective for latency with an explicit exception for "Complex Payloads" (e.g., long sequences or streaming).
- The proposed credit schedule in Resilience_Rider_Draft.docx is acceptable if we cap cumulative credits per 12-month period and exclude credits for scheduled maintenance with >=72 hours notice.
- Order form: ensure product SKUs map to the correct capacity tier and include a short clause that allows Redwood to route to a compatible model variant during regional degradation (this preserves graceful degradation and reduces outage risk).

I’ll generate a redline that tightens the definitions and adds the maintenance notice language. Sergio — once I send the legal redline, can you coordinate with Helios procurement for a targeted 48-hour review window? We need to keep to their pilot timeline.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Legal_comments_helios_redlines.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Final resilience rider and order form (for DocuSign routing)

Hi Susan / Procurement team —

Please find a consolidated clean copy attached: Resilience_Rider_Final.docx and Orderform_HeliosDX_v1.json. Key changes since the draft:

- Availability: 99.95% monthly (primary region), pilot month telemetry and runbook deliverable included as evidence.
- Latency: P50 < 120ms and P95 < 350ms for "Standard Payloads" (<=512 input tokens, <=256 output tokens). "Complex Payloads" excluded and subject to model-variant routing.
- Credits: tiered credit schedule with 12-month cap, excludes scheduled maintenance with 72 hours notice and force majeure.
- Regional failover: optional add-on reflected in the order form (SKU: HX-FALLBACK-01) with pricing uplift shown.

Next steps: Procurement, if you confirm the DocuSign route we will upload the final rider and push for signature. If procurement needs a one-page summary for internal approvers, Kim and I can produce that within 24 hours.

Thanks — looking forward to closing the pilot.

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[sent on behalf of Redwood Inference]
